body.statement:
For every \(j\in\mathbb N\), \(C_{\alpha,j}(Z)\) is a measurable interval and satisfies
\[
\inf_{x\in\mathcal M_{T,m}}\Pr_x\{\ell(x)\in C_{\alpha,j}(Z)\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]
Its half-length is within the factor \(1+j^{-1}\) of the infimum over the positive-standard-deviation affine modulus intervals. Define
\[
r_\alpha=\sqrt{\log\{1+(1-2\alpha)^2\}},
\qquad
c_\alpha=\frac{(1-2\alpha)r_\alpha}{2},
\qquad
z_\alpha=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2).
\]
Then
\[
c_\alpha\,\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)
\le\operatorname{EL}^{\star}_\alpha
\le\liminf_{j\to\infty}\sup_{x\in\mathcal M_{T,m}}
\mathbb E_x[\operatorname{length}C_{\alpha,j}(Z)]
\le(1+2z_\alpha)\,\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1).
\]
The lower bound is over measurable interval-valued procedures.
body.justification: The result turns the same exact nested modulus into an everywhere-defined bias-aware interval with exact finite-sample coverage and explicit global expected-length constants.
body.gap: Armstrong and Kolesar optimize Gaussian intervals for supplied operators; this theorem applies the total measurable construction to the nested staggered-DiD score law and states the measurable interval class needed by the lower bound.
body.consumer: Researchers obtain a computable honest interval and a certified expected-length benchmark even when the modulus is nondifferentiable.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(j\), and abbreviate \(r=r_{\mathrm{CI},j}\), \(b=b_r\), and \(s=s_r>0\). The exact Gaussian score law and the exact-bias part of the total-modulus rule imply that, for every \(x\in\mathcal M_{T,m}\),
\[
\frac{\widehat\theta_r-\ell(x)}s\sim\mathcal N(t_x,1),
\qquad |t_x|\le b/s. \tag{9}
\]
For fixed \(c\ge0\), the function
\[
p_c(t)=\Pr\{|\mathcal N(t,1)|\le c\}=\Phi(c-t)-\Phi(-c-t)
\]
is even. For \(t\ge0\), differentiation gives \(p_c'(t)=-\phi(c-t)+\phi(c+t)\le0\), because \(|c-t|\le c+t\) and the standard-normal density decreases with absolute value. Thus (9) and the definition of \(\operatorname{cv}_\alpha\) give
\[
\Pr_x\{\ell(x)\in C_{\alpha,j}(Z)\}
=p_{\operatorname{cv}_\alpha(b/s)}(t_x)
\ge p_{\operatorname{cv}_\alpha(b/s)}(b/s)
\ge1-\alpha.
\]
The deterministic half-length is \(s_r\operatorname{cv}_\alpha(b_r/s_r)\). Its claimed factor \(1+j^{-1}\) optimality is exactly the defining inequality for \(r_{\mathrm{CI},j}\).

For the upper expected-length bound, the unit-radius admissibility lemma permits \(r=1\) as a competitor. The event \(|\mathcal N(0,1)|\le z_\alpha\) has probability \(1-\alpha\), and the triangle inequality shows
\[
\{|\mathcal N(0,1)|\le z_\alpha\}
\subseteq
\{|\mathcal N(t,1)|\le t+z_\alpha\}
\qquad(t\ge0).
\]
Hence \(\operatorname{cv}_\alpha(t)\le t+z_\alpha\). With \(b_1\le\omega(1)/2\) and \(s_1\le\omega(1)\), where again \(\omega=\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}\),
\[
2s_1\operatorname{cv}_\alpha(b_1/s_1)
\le2b_1+2z_\alpha s_1
\le(1+2z_\alpha)\omega(1). \tag{10}
\]
The infimum-approaching property of \(r_{\mathrm{CI},j}\), followed by \(j\to\infty\), proves the final upper bound. Every \(C_{\alpha,j}\) is admissible for the definition of \(\operatorname{EL}_\alpha^\star\), so the middle inequality follows.

It remains to prove the lower bound for an arbitrary measurable interval procedure \(C\) with uniform coverage at least \(1-\alpha\). Since \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\),
\[
0<r_\alpha=\sqrt{\log\{1+(1-2\alpha)^2\}}<1.
\]
Let \(x^-_{r_\alpha},x^+_{r_\alpha}\) be the canonical modulus endpoints, let \(P_-\) and \(P_+\) be their score laws, and set \(\Delta=\omega(r_\alpha)\). The same direct Gaussian likelihood-ratio and Cauchy--Schwarz calculation as in the minimax proof gives
\[
\operatorname{TV}(P_+,P_-)
\le\frac12\sqrt{\exp(r_\alpha^2)-1}
=\frac{1-2\alpha}{2}. \tag{11}
\]
Write \(A_-\) and \(A_+\) for the events that \(C(Z)\) contains \(\ell(x^-_{r_\alpha})\) and \(\ell(x^+_{r_\alpha})\), respectively. Honesty and total variation imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_-(A_-\cap A_+)
&\ge1-P_-(A_-^c)-P_-(A_+^c)\\
&\ge1-\alpha-\{P_+(A_+^c)+\operatorname{TV}(P_+,P_-)\}\\
&\ge1-2\alpha-\operatorname{TV}(P_+,P_-)\\
&\ge\frac{1-2\alpha}{2}. \tag{12}
\end{aligned}
\]
Because \(C(Z)\) is an interval, its length is at least \(\Delta\) on \(A_-\cap A_+\). Equations (11)--(12) yield
\[
\sup_x\mathbb E_x[\operatorname{length}C(Z)]
\ge\mathbb E_{P_-}[\operatorname{length}C(Z)]
\ge\frac{1-2\alpha}{2}\omega(r_\alpha). \tag{13}
\]
Concavity of the nonnegative modulus gives
\[
\omega(r_\alpha)\ge r_\alpha\omega(1)+(1-r_\alpha)\omega(0)
\ge r_\alpha\omega(1).
\]
Substitution into (13), followed by the infimum over all honest measurable interval-valued \(C\), proves \(\operatorname{EL}_\alpha^\star\ge c_\alpha\omega(1)\). The argument used only the exact nested modulus, so it makes no calendar-rate claim.
